content:
Two years ago when Apple launched the M4 Mac mini, teardown reports quickly brought good news: the built-in SSD was not soldered to the motherboard. Users could buy upgrade accessories on the market, and we even filmed a tutorial showing how to do it.

However, the newly released M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini appear to have the storage chips soldered back onto the motherboard.

The new Mac mini's storage chips being soldered on again is a step backwards

Expand Mac mini revealed in a blog post that the NAND chips are soldered directly onto the motherboard, similar to the situation with the M1 and M2 Mac mini. This means the SSD module can no longer be removed.

Expand Mac mini sells storage upgrade modules for the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini. However, they stated that "it looks very difficult to support the M6 and M5 Pro at this stage."

Without a slot, there's nothing to replace, and the room for us to work with is very limited. In August this year, we mentioned that we would expand support after testing the actual machines. The test results are now out, and they are not what we had hoped for. We will continue to look for solutions, but support for the M6 and M5 Pro looks unlikely. If the situation changes, we will notify everyone immediately.

For comparison, Expand Mac mini's 1TB SSD expansion module for the M4 Mac mini sells for USD 300. Apple charges USD 500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini's 2TB module costs USD 420, while Apple's upgrade option costs USD 1,000.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple's repair guide still shows that the SSD can be removed. We have not yet seen any teardown report confirming this claim.

If you're using an M4 Mac mini and want to upgrade storage, you can refer to the detailed tutorial produced by 9to5Mac's Jeff Benjamin.

Although it's not the same as upgrading internal storage, Satechi has launched a cleverly designed accessory that combines an SSD enclosure with additional ports, made specifically for the M6 Mac mini.
